title: First Word All Beings Say Bismillah Through The Language Of Their State

questions.question: What question is raised at the start of the passage about all beings saying “In the Name of Allah”?
questions.answer: It asks whether this claim is really true.

questions.question: What example is used to show that a single person moving a whole town by force cannot be acting alone?
questions.answer: The example is a soldier who carries out authority on behalf of a ruler and government rather than by personal strength.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the example of the soldier?
questions.answer: Visible power and authority in great tasks point to acting under a higher command.

questions.question: How do seeds and grains function as signs in the argument?
questions.answer: Though tiny, they produce huge trees, which shows they work through divine power, not their own limited ability.

questions.question: What do trees provide for people in this explanation?
questions.answer: They bring out provisions and benefits from divine mercy and place them before us.

questions.question: How are gardens described in relation to divine power?
questions.answer: They are presented like places where many kinds of nourishment are prepared by Allah’s power.

questions.question: Which animals are mentioned as examples of blessed creatures, and what do they provide?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, sheep, and goats are mentioned, and they provide pure milk.

questions.question: Why is milk presented as a special sign of mercy?
questions.answer: It is described as pure, nourishing, and gently provided for living beings through Allah’s care.

questions.question: What surprising action of roots and rootlets is emphasized?
questions.answer: Their soft structure still lets them pass through hard soil and even rock.

questions.question: What does the passage say becomes subject to things when Allah’s name is invoked?
questions.answer: Hardness and resistance in creation become obedient to divine command.

questions.question: How do roots and leaves challenge a purely naturalistic explanation of the world?
questions.answer: Their delicate form accomplishing powerful results shows that blind material forces are not enough to explain what happens.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the whole passage?
questions.answer: All created things work under Allah’s command and display His power, mercy, and authority.

questions.question: In this passage, what does “the tongue of disposition” mean in simple terms?
questions.answer: It means that things declare Allah’s power by what they do and how they are made, even without spoken words.

questions.question: Why would a person assume that someone forcing a whole town to work must have official backing?
questions.answer: Because one individual does not have enough personal power or authority for that kind of task.

questions.question: How does that comparison help explain the actions of created things?
questions.answer: It shows that creation carries out amazing works through Allah’s authority, not independent power.

questions.question: What do tiny seeds suggest about the relationship between size and power?
questions.answer: Small size does not limit what can happen when divine power is behind it.

questions.question: How are trees portrayed as serving human beings?
questions.answer: They gather and deliver beneficial provisions to people as part of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What image is used for gardens, and what does that image suggest?
questions.answer: Gardens are pictured like cooking places full of prepared foods, showing abundance and planning.

questions.question: What does the mention of milk-producing animals add to the overall message?
questions.answer: It gives a familiar daily example of how Allah sends provision through living creatures.

questions.question: Why does the passage focus on the softness of roots and rootlets?
questions.answer: To highlight the contrast between their weakness and the hard matter they pass through.

questions.question: What point is made by comparing roots in rock with branches in air?
questions.answer: Producing fruit in hard conditions is made just as easy as in open space by divine command.

questions.question: How do leaves standing against heat deepen the argument?
questions.answer: They show that delicate things can remain protected even in harsh conditions because Allah controls those conditions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of referring to Musa’s staff and Ibrahim in the passage?
questions.answer: These references connect natural signs to well-known examples of Allah overruling normal physical expectations.

questions.question: What attitude toward the natural world does this passage teach?
questions.answer: It teaches believers to see creation as obedient to Allah and full of signs of His mercy and power.

questions.question: What is being confirmed in the opening lines of the target passage?
questions.answer: The truth that all beings, in their own created way, act with reference to Allah’s name.

questions.question: Why is the image of one person controlling a whole town persuasive?
questions.answer: It makes clear that extraordinary effects require authority and support beyond the individual.

questions.question: In that example, what two things does the soldier depend on?
questions.answer: He depends on the ruler’s power and the government’s authority.

questions.question: What parallel is made between the soldier and created things?
questions.answer: Just as the soldier acts under higher authority, all things act under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What do seeds and grains reveal about the source of their ability?
questions.answer: Their ability to carry the beginning of huge trees shows that their power comes from Allah.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do trees and gardens do for people?
questions.answer: They provide food and other benefits as channels of divine generosity.

questions.question: What makes the milk from certain animals an important example?
questions.answer: It comes as a clean and life-giving provision through creatures that serve human needs.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relation between roots and hard earth?
questions.answer: Soft roots move through resistant ground in a way that points to divine subjection of matter.

questions.question: Who is directly criticized in the later part of the passage?
questions.answer: People who explain reality only through nature and ignore Allah’s command are criticized.

questions.question: What argument is made against relying on heat and hardness as ultimate causes?
questions.answer: These forces are themselves under command and cannot act independently of Allah.

questions.question: Why are Qur’anic miracles brought into the discussion here?
questions.answer: They illustrate that what looks impossible becomes possible when Allah commands it.

questions.question: What central belief should a reader strengthen after reading this passage?
questions.answer: The reader should strengthen trust that all creation operates through Allah’s will, not by self-sufficient causes.

questions.question: What claim about all beings is examined in this passage?
questions.answer: The claim is that all beings, by their state and actions, point to acting in Allah’s name.

questions.question: What human situation is used as an analogy to make this claim easier to understand?
questions.answer: A situation where one man appears to control and direct an entire town.

questions.question: Why would a person not believe that such a man acted purely by himself?
questions.answer: Because the scale of the work shows borrowed authority and power.

questions.question: What does this analogy suggest about the activities of the natural world?
questions.answer: It suggests they are carried out through divine authority behind them.

questions.question: How does the passage use the contrast between tiny seeds and massive trees?
questions.answer: It uses that contrast to show that limited physical size cannot explain the result by itself.

questions.question: What role do trees have in relation to mercy?
questions.answer: They receive and pass on provisions from Allah’s mercy to human beings.

questions.question: How are gardens presented as more than just patches of plants?
questions.answer: They are shown as places where many forms of sustenance are prepared and offered.

questions.question: What does the example of grazing animals teach about provision?
questions.answer: Allah sends pure nourishment through ordinary animals in a way full of wisdom and care.

questions.question: Why is the movement of soft roots through rock so significant?
questions.answer: It overturns the expectation that weakness cannot overcome hardness.

questions.question: What broader point is made by the survival of delicate leaves in intense heat?
questions.answer: Conditions that seem overpowering are still controlled by Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage respond to people who reduce everything to natural forces?
questions.answer: It presents living signs that such forces are not independent masters but governed means.

questions.question: If a student had to state the passage’s message in one sentence, what would be a good summary?
questions.answer: The whole created world shows that Allah’s command gives power, order, and provision to things that could never manage these on their own.

questions.question: What is the main issue addressed by the short question at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: It addresses whether creation truly bears witness to acting in Allah’s name.

questions.question: What does the example of the town teach about unseen authority?
questions.answer: Great visible effects can prove the presence of hidden backing and command.

questions.question: In the analogy, why is the man identified as a soldier rather than an independent actor?
questions.answer: Because his success depends on delegated authority and support from a ruler.

questions.question: How does this analogy prepare the reader to think about seeds, gardens, and animals?
questions.answer: It trains the reader to look beyond outward forms and recognize divine agency.

questions.question: What do seeds and grains do that makes them powerful evidence in the passage?
questions.answer: They carry the beginning of large trees despite their tiny form.

questions.question: What is being emphasized when trees are described as offering what they receive from mercy?
questions.answer: They are servants delivering provision, not owners producing it by themselves.

questions.question: Why are gardens linked with many different foods?
questions.answer: Their variety shows rich planning, generosity, and organized provision from Allah.

questions.question: What quality of milk makes it especially meaningful in the passage?
questions.answer: Its purity and suitability for nourishment show refined mercy in provision.

questions.question: What does the success of soft rootlets in hard ground imply about physical obstacles?
questions.answer: Obstacles are not absolute barriers when Allah commands otherwise.

questions.question: How do the examples of roots and leaves work together in the argument?
questions.answer: Both show that what appears weak can prevail over what appears strong through divine command.

questions.question: What is the effect of the Qur’anic references in the final paragraph of the target passage?
questions.answer: They connect the signs in nature with revealed reminders of Allah’s power over creation.

questions.question: What kind of worldview is the reader being called to adopt?
questions.answer: A worldview that sees creation as obedient, meaningful, and constantly pointing to Allah.

questions.question: What statement from earlier is brought back and questioned at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: The statement that all beings, through their condition, say “In the Name of Allah.”

questions.question: How is the answer to that question given first: by abstract theory or by concrete example?
questions.answer: It is given first through a concrete example.

questions.question: What is the concrete example meant to prove?
questions.answer: It is meant to prove that remarkable action points to authority beyond the visible agent.

questions.question: How does the passage move from the human example to the rest of creation?
questions.answer: It says the same principle applies to all things in the world.

questions.question: Why are seeds and grains especially useful examples for this point?
questions.answer: They are very small, yet they hold and produce outcomes far beyond their apparent capacity.

questions.question: What do trees and gardens reveal about Allah besides power?
questions.answer: They also reveal His mercy and generosity in feeding creation.

questions.question: What do cows, camels, sheep, and goats reveal through what they give?
questions.answer: They reveal that Allah sends gentle and beneficial provision through living creatures.

questions.question: Why is the image of silk-like roots important to the passage’s logic?
questions.answer: It sharpens the contrast between softness and the hard materials they penetrate.

questions.question: What does the phrase about everything becoming subjected to them mean in context?
questions.answer: It means resistance in nature is overcome because Allah makes things obedient to His command.

questions.question: How is the confidence of those who trust only in material causes challenged?
questions.answer: The passage shows that the very forces they rely on are themselves under divine rule.

questions.question: What do the examples related to Musa and Ibrahim add to the discussion of roots and leaves?
questions.answer: They show that Allah can make hard things open and harmful things become harmless.

questions.question: What spiritual habit of mind does this passage encourage in a believer?
questions.answer: It encourages seeing ordinary natural processes as signs of Allah’s active power, mercy, and command.
